findings.title: Passkey conditional UI is not set up when user is null, breaking passwordless login
findings.body: In authenticate(), the call to webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) is now guarded by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()). This method returns false when context.getUser() is null (its condition includes user != null). Previously, fillContextForm was performed when user == null (inside the else block). As a result, on the normal login page with no pre-selected user, passkey conditional UI is never set up, so users cannot use passkeys for passwordless login. Existing tests for initial login (e.g., passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey) will fail. The guard should not require user != null; it should be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`.

findings.title: Passkey conditional UI no longer added on error challenges when user is null
findings.body: In the challenge() override, the condition changed from `context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires user != null. This means when an error occurs during initial authentication (user not set), passkeys will not be filled into the challenge response, so the conditional UI disappears on error pages. The original intent was to fill passkeys when user is null; the new condition reverses that. This breaks the error flow for passwordless login.
